ca_mindless_mound.blurb: A small outcrop in the Lost Horse part of Joshua Tree National Park, tucked just beyond the south side of a larger formation and reached by a flat walk of around five minutes. All twelve routes are trad. The spread is friendly: most lines fall between 5.7 and 5.10, with a few easier starters, one 5.9 and a single 5.11 for the experienced. The wall sits in shade during the morning and picks up sun through the afternoon, so it suits a warm day when you want to start cool. Modest in scale and rarely a destination by itself, it works well as a quick add-on to a day around Lost Horse.

ca_attitude_wall.blurb: The standout wall of the North Area at Devil's Punchbowl, in the high desert east of the Los Angeles basin. About 90 feet tall, it holds twelve bolted sport lines. The east side stands vertical to overhanging and carries the hardest climbing in the low to mid 5.12s, while the gentler slab on the west flank and the southeast end hold the 5.10s and 5.11s plus a lone 5.9. Expect little at the easy end: this is a place for climbers already comfortable on 5.10 and up. Footing at the base is uneven and the rock can shed a few loose pieces, so a helmet is sensible.
ca_attitude_wall.approach: Follow the North Area trail and, shortly before reaching Little Attitude Wall, take a side path heading east to the south end of the wall. Continue along the base past the southeast face to reach the central and right-hand lines.

ca_owl_the_2.blurb: A slab on the southwest side of the Middle Earth valley at Fairview Mountain, in the high desert near Apple Valley. Locals sometimes call it the Guide Wall. It faces east and holds a dozen routes, mostly bolted with a couple of trad lines. The grades lean easy: a cluster of 5.7s, a handful from 5.6 to 5.9, one 5.3 and a single 5.10, which makes it a sensible spot for newer leaders and anyone warming up. It lies southwest of the Sidewinder wall, and reaching it means a hike up into the valley.

ca_crossfire_crag.blurb: One of the better walls in the Box Canyon East part of New Jack City, in the high desert near Barstow. It is a tall, east-facing sport crag with twelve routes that stay in view of your vehicle. The wall gets morning sun and afternoon shade. Several of the lines are long and sustained, and the grades sit well above beginner level: a single 5.9 and 5.10 at the low end, then a solid block of 5.11s and 5.12s, topped by one 5.13. The walk from the end of the road is short, only a few minutes up a good hillside trail.

ca_pea_brain.blurb: A rounded dome in East Wonderland Valley, set behind Freak Brothers Dome in the Wonderland of Rocks, Joshua Tree National Park. It is a minor crag rather than a destination, but a decent way to dodge the crowds. Of its twelve climbs, eight are trad and four are top-rope. The bulk are moderate face routes, with six at 5.9, plus a few easier and a few 5.10s, and one extreme trad line at the very top of the scale. Routes on the main face lose their sun early on winter afternoons because a neighbouring dome casts shade across the base.

ca_diamondback_area.blurb: A sport-climbing sector in the Lower Gorge of Owens River Gorge, near Bishop. Eleven routes are bolted sport and one is a top-rope. The grades favor intermediates: three at 5.7, a scattering of 5.8 to 5.10, and five at 5.11. It is a moderate crag for people who want classic gorge climbing without 5.12 difficulty. The setting is a river canyon lined with cottonwoods, though the power plant and its pylons and pipework intrude on the atmosphere. This end of the gorge sees fewer people than many other parts.

ca_old_woman_east_face_the.blurb: The side of the Old Woman formation that looks onto Hidden Valley Campground in Joshua Tree National Park. A dozen trad routes cover the range from easy to difficult: a pair of 5.7s and two 5.8s, four 5.10s, two 5.11s and two 5.12s. Several are well-known crack and face lines that draw steady traffic, so expect company on the popular ones. Because it stands right beside the campground, the trail to the base is easy and short, and the formation makes a convenient place to start or finish a day in the Hidden Valley area.

ca_labor_dome.blurb: A small dome in the Outback section of the Hidden Valley area, Joshua Tree National Park. Roughly ten minutes of walking from the road takes you to the base. The twelve routes are mainly trad, with two top-rope options. Difficulty is gentle overall: most climbs run from about 5.5 to 5.9, with four at 5.9, plus a lone 5.10 and a single 5.11, and one easy scramble. The wall generally faces south, so it collects sun and is a good pick on a cold day.
